title: Agents template: tool allow-list, timeout wrappers, and JSON schema validation for tool outputs
author: Dana Lo
body: Summary: This PR introduces the v1 Agents quickstart template (TypeScript) focused on safe tool calling patterns and production defaults. Key additions are (1) a strict tool allow-list with explicit naming, (2) a timeout + cancellation wrapper for all tool executions (per-tool and global), and (3) JSON-schema validation of tool outputs with clear, typed error handling. Motivation: In dogfooding and early customer trials we saw two recurring failure modes: agents calling unintended tools (or calling intended tools with unsafe inputs) and downstream failures caused by tools returning unstructured / unexpected payloads. This template establishes the "production shape" we want: predictable tool behavior, bounded execution time, and validated outputs that can be safely fed back into the model. What’s included: - Tool registry with allow-list enforcement (default deny). - Tool execution wrapper that: (a) enforces timeouts via AbortController, (b) captures structured errors (tool_error_class + tool_name), (c) emits tracing span events for start/finish/failure with redacted inputs, and (d) ensures we never log tool args/results by default. - Output validation using JSON Schema (Ajv) with human-readable error messages and safe truncation. - Example tools: "search_docs" (stub) and "get_ticket" (stub) to illustrate the registry pattern; both are intentionally non-networked by default and safe for local runs. - Example agent loop with Redwood Hosted API tool calling format and guardrails for parsing. - Docs: README sections for configuring allow-lists, timeouts, and adding new tools; includes guidance for PII and logging hygiene. Backwards compatibility: N/A (new template). Config: - REDWOOD_TOOL_ALLOWLIST: comma-separated list of tool names; if unset, the template starts with an empty allow-list and logs a warning on startup with guidance. - REDWOOD_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS (default 5000) and per-tool override via tool definition. - REDWOOD_TOOL_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES (default 32KB) to prevent runaway tool payloads. Notes / future work (out of scope): streaming reconnect patterns and SDK helper consolidation are handled in ENG-2847; telemetry contract validations will come in ENG-2845. Checklist: - [x] Tool allow-list default deny - [x] Timeouts/cancellation for tools - [x] JSON schema validation for tool outputs - [x] Unit tests for registry/validator - [x] README + extension guidance - [x] Minimal lint + CI wiring for template package

review_conversation:
Monica Patel (review): Can we be explicit that tool outputs must be JSON-serializable and validated before being re-injected into the model? Also, please confirm we don’t log tool args/results by default.
Dana Lo (author): Updated README to state outputs must be JSON-serializable and validated; also added a callout in logging.ts and ensured registry wrapper logs only tool_name + duration + status (no args/results).

Marcus Lin (review): Default deny allow-list is good, but starting with an empty allow-list may confuse users. Can we fail fast with a clear error? Also, make sure env parsing trims whitespace and rejects unknown tool names.
Dana Lo (author): Added startup warning + actionable message in README and console output; also added strict parsing with trimming and an "unknown tool" error that lists allowed names when the allow-list contains an unregistered tool. Kept empty allow-list as a safe default but now the sample .env includes the two example tools to make the happy path obvious.

Allison Grant (review): Please add trace attributes for tool spans (tool.name, tool.timeout_ms, tool.status) and ensure cardinality is bounded.
Dana Lo (author): Added tool.name (string from registry), tool.timeout_ms (number), tool.status (success|error|timeout|not_allowed). No dynamic attributes from tool args or results.

Sean Gallagher (review): Timeout default of 5s seems OK, but the wrapper should ensure timers are cleared and that timeouts are distinguishable from tool exceptions. Also consider a max output size to avoid huge payloads blowing up memory.
Dana Lo (author): Implemented ToolTimeoutError with error_class=tool_timeout and ensured timers are cleared in finally. Added REDWOOD_TOOL_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES default 32768 and truncation + validation error when exceeded.

Wei Chen (review): README: please add a short section on "How to add a new tool" with a concrete example and mention PII guidance.
Dana Lo (author): Added a step-by-step guide with a sample tool definition including schema, timeout override, and redaction note; also added a PII guidance section and linked it to "don’t log tool args/results".
